newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian hard left, government hold "useful" talks.
newsitem.headline: Italian hard left, government hold "useful" talks.

text.p: The leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation said on Thursday that talks with the main party in the centre-left coalition to try to resolve potentially destabilising differences had been useful.
"The climate is constructive," Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said after a two and a half hour meeting with Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) head Massimo D'Alema.
PDS sources meanwhile said the meeting between the two "basically went well".

A joint statement issued by the two men later said they discussed "open questions facing parliament and on which there have been difficulties in the coalition in recent days" and described the meeting as "polite and constructive".

Bertinotti brushed aside questions about whether the survival of the centre-left government, which does not include Refoundation but depends on the hard-left party for its majority in the lower house of parliament, was in danger.
"One can say that the political intention is to make this coalition live in self-sufficient terms," he said.
Armando Cossutta, Refoundation parliamentary leader, said he believed "there are the conditions for an agreement".
"Naturally, differences remain but there is certainly not the sense of a showdown," he added.

Bertinotti has met leading government figures in recent days to try to resolve deep differences between his party and the ruling coalition over a planned mini-budget, privatisations and a reform of the welfare state.
Bertinotti said he and D'Alema discussed issues linked to the privatisation of state telecommunications company Stet and electricity giant Enel as well as assessing the political climate.
The joint statement said no decision was taken during the meeting and no position taken over budgetary matters or the mini-budget, which was not even discussed.
"The meeting was useful," said Bertinotti, adding that the time was ripe for a meeting of all the centre-left coalition forces to discuss pressing problems such as jobs.
PDS sources said D'Alema had assured Bertinotti that the government had no intention of realigning itself.

The centre-right Freedom Alliance of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi has recently put out feelers to Prodi's government, offering its support "in the country's interest" to pass legislation opposed by Refoundation.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has pledged to introduce a mini-budget in the coming weeks with up to 14.6 trillion lire ($8.5 billion) of deficit-cutting measures.

Bertinotti has already said he will not accept tax hikes or cuts to welfare spending, drastically limiting Prodi's options as he fights to contain the state deficit and book Italy a place on the launch of the single European currency.
The government and Refoundation are also negotiating over the planned sale later this year of Stet, to which the hard left is ideologically opposed.
The privatisation still needs parliamentary legislation and without a deal between Prodi and Bertinotti, the long delayed sell-off would be doomed to another postponement.

The two men met later on Thursday, along with Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico and Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni.
